_about: Persistent memory for the drift detector (kb/_build_governance_candidates.py). 'mapped' = this surface is ALREADY covered by an existing register row. 'dismissed' = it needs no row, and why. Anything in neither is proposed as a candidate. Dismissal lives here, not in a database, so the REASON is reviewable in a diff and cannot silently diverge from the register it annotates.

dismissed.workflow:docket-process.yml: The Docket's processor (#2963 step 3; Sam's go in session 2026-11-09, "yes, start step 3", on the order Sky set out on #2963). A writer acting without a session: it carries out rulings a reviewer saved on Docket cases (field:kb_curation.docket_ruling). It adds no decision right: each case names the register row that owns its decision (`dr`), the ruling is that owner deciding, and the job runs only the commands the reviewed kb/docket/cases.json names for the choice ruled, only scripts on kb/_docket_process.py's ALLOWED list (each writes committed files it can undo from its own receipt), only with --apply beside --expect. It writes a receipt with its undo under kb/docket/receipts/ and commits to main behind the daily build (concurrency daily-dashboard). Nothing on the decision sheets' hold list reaches it.
dismissed.function:docket-process: The Commons' "Process my rulings now" (#2963 step 3, Sam's go 2026-11-09). Reads no table and writes nothing; its one action is dispatching docket-process.yml on main, for a signed-in reviewer only (rpc/is_allowed_reviewer), with a token the browser never holds. What runs is bounded by workflow:docket-process.yml's own entry.
dismissed.field:kb_curation.docket_ruling: A ruling on a Docket case (#2963 step 2, Sam's go 2026-11-09). The field adds no decision right: each case in kb/docket/cases.json names the register row that owns its decision (`dr`, checked by tests/docket_rulings_test.py), and the ruling is that row's owner deciding. It is written by a signed-in reviewer under their own name (kb_curation's insert and update policies), is read by kb/_docket_rulings.py, and changes nothing by itself: a session (step 3: the processor) carries it out with the case's plan and files a receipt.

dismissed.rpc:cpl_library_set_public: The public Library's writer and its read (Sam, 2026-10-20: "a public library I can copy them over to and set view permissions in the Admin tab"; "Mock up looks great!"). cpl_library_set_public() takes the team phrase or a reviewer sign-in (Sam, 2026-10-23 18:50Z, his own call, reversing his 2026-10-20 reviewer-only call: "can you set the Library page to be editable with Team phrase and not just magic link? I want the team to be able to make their artifacts public on the public library"), and records who listed; a trigger refuses the public columns written any other way, and the history trigger files every prior row, so a listing is reversible from the database (Rule 10 a2). Its read, cpl_library_public(), is open to anon on purpose for the public page (library/index.html) and Sierra, and returns only listed, current, linked rows marked Public, and only public fields: title, kind, occasion, date, a public summary, topics and the link. Notes, briefs, made_by, rebuild_from, versions, the internal summary and every name stay behind the team phrase. It carries no student or staff detail, so the student-detail disclosure ADR does not reach it. The decision right is Sam's, exercised by the team he gave the phrase to or by a reviewer sign-in, so it needs no register row; unlisting is the safe direction and follows any retire or narrowed audience. A Claude page also needs its own link set public in claude.ai, which COBI cannot set or check, so the switch asks the lister to confirm it.
dismissed.table:cpl_library: The Library tab's register of decks, films and documents (Sam, 2026-10-05: build it; files live in the team Drive). Each row is a link and its metadata, never the file. Read and written only under the team phrase or a reviewer sign-in (team_pass_ok() or is_allowed_reviewer()), the same audience as the tab; no anon read, no delete policy, delete and truncate revoked. Every edit files the prior row in cpl_library_history through a trigger, so a write is reversible from the database (Rule 10 a2). It carries no student or staff detail beyond the name a teammate types as added_by or updated_by. Since 2026-10-23 (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 120, cards 2 to 7, each his own call) a row also says who the piece is made for: for_kind (college, district, agency, vendor, the Chancellor's Office, or a typed Other category in for_category) and for_name, an organization's name the title already carries, never a person's; the public read returns them, so the public page can filter by them. The same writers under the same gate, so no new decision right: Make a visual on the tab writes a college's record pair the way the CPL Opportunity side sessions filed the first twelve. Who decides a piece's audience is Sam: a public file with no audience set shows under Needs attention until he rules, so the decision right already has its owner and needs no register row. A second writer, the session-side filer scripts/library_file.py (Sam's calls 7-8, 2026-10-05), records each file it puts in Drive: a receipt applied as a named migration, guarded on the Drive file id so a second apply changes nothing, under updated_by library-filer@bot, with the history trigger keeping the prior row. It writes the link, the version list and home, moves a Requested record to Draft on its first draft and changes no other status, and never sets an audience, so Sam's two decision rights stay his. Since S459 (Sam's Sheet 121 card 1, 2026-10-23) a row also says whether the piece's substance is knowledge and links its KB note (knowledge, kb_note); the same writers under the same gate, no new decision right. Since S490 (Sam, 2026-10-26: "I want to make sure I can Regenerate a visual when I either add a document or note to it") a row also carries the documents a piece is built from (sources: a link, or a document's text a teammate pastes in; the tab's help says never a student's record) and an open rebuild request (regen: who asked, when, whether the draft replaces a public copy at once, the draft's link, who approved it). The same writers under the same gate, and the history trigger files both; replacing a public copy stays the decision of whoever approves the draft on the card, which the request records, so no new decision right.

dismissed.table:program_record_verdicts: A reviewer's reading of a program record (Confirm or Needs a fix), written from the Program Requirements tab's Records view. Sam ruled the write himself (Open Asks Sheet 51 card 1, 'build', 2026-10-08, on the mock-up Program Records Review). The gate is technical and stated: program_record_verdict_add writes, as an allowed reviewer (is_allowed_reviewer()), with the session's email, never an argument. The one other writer is the re-read function, which carries a reviewer's confirm across a rerun that changes only the totals and the degree's figures, every block the same, as a new row in that reviewer's name naming the verdict it carries (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 82 card 1, 'carry', 2026-10-14). The criterion is written down: the tab's four checks, three of them machine checks the server applies (program_record_machine_pass), and Confirm turns a record checked only while the fingerprint of the requirements the page showed still matches. The log is append-only (reads only for the page's roles; undo is a new row), and a Needs a fix note lands on the college's reading procedure through program_source_procedure_set, whose history keeps the prior record. It names staff emails, so the read is reviewer-only; it holds no student grain, so the student-detail ADR does not reach it. Decision owner: the CPL Initiative (Sam).

dismissed.workflow:program-requirements-college.ym: Phase 2 of the program requirements harvest: every program at one college, run on a dispatch or a commit marked [read], [extract] or [load], never on a schedule. It reads the college's public catalog from a runner under Sam's sheet-23 call 5, and its load job writes only program_requirement_records, through program_requirement_records_college_load(), which inserts each record unchecked, never touches a row already there, and answers the service role alone; a person's Confirm on the Records view is the only way a record becomes checked and reaches Sierra; the public reads every record since Sam's Open Asks Sheet 67 (2026-10-12), each unchecked one marked Not yet confirmed. Public catalog data with no staff or student detail (Sam, 2026-10-04: "No need for governance at this point. Everything is public record"). Each load commits a receipt naming the keys it inserted, which is how it rolls back. Its reread step (S389, a dispatch with step=reread, never a push; Sam's Open Asks Sheet 78 card 2, "Record both figures", which re-reads records) writes through program_requirement_records_college_reread(), which replaces a row only while it is unchecked and an earlier run read it (a person's reading of an unchecked row no longer holds it, S392), never writes checked or display, and answers the service role alone; where the row's latest verdict is a confirm of the record it replaces and the rerun changes only the totals and the degree's figures, it adds the carried confirm to program_record_verdicts in the reviewer's name (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 82 card 1, 'carry'); its receipt holds each replaced row's before-values and the carried keys, and its rollback restores them unchecked and deletes the carried rows. Its display job (S356, a dispatch with step=display, never a push) writes program_requirement_records.display alone, from the committed receipt of the build the page carries, after Sam's go on a display build (his sheet 42 card 2 practice; 2026-10-10 "Yes build" for 5be53871ebf4); it reads each row's build first and commits the applied record, which is the rollback.

dismissed.workflow:supabase-migrate.yml: The runner-applied migration (Sam, 2026-10-13: "Build the runner with or without my approvals"; Open Asks Sheet 74 card 2, "allow", 17:51Z, for this entry). It applies one committed SQL file under chatbox/, kb/ or supabase/, named by kb/migrations/.apply, only on a claude/** push whose trigger file differs from main's, never on a merge commit or a schedule, in the GitHub environment "database" (a required reviewer there makes each apply wait for that person). dismissed.function:workplan-rebuild: The build queue behind an Annual Goals save (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 75 card 2, "both", 2026-10-13 19:18Z, on a card that named this as a new write path with a governance entry). The Edge Function writes no table; its one action is a dispatch of daily-dashboard.yml on main, a run the build's cadence (CA-01) already allows by hand, idempotent and serialized by its concurrency group, and it reuses a build already queued, pending or waiting. It asks PostgREST, as the caller, is_allowed_reviewer() or team_pass_ok(), so only those DR-13 already lets edit the workplan can queue one; the anon key alone is refused. Its GitHub key (WORKPLAN_DISPATCH_TOKEN, Actions read and write on this repository only) is an Edge Function secret Sam sets; without it the function answers 503 and the page says tonight, as before. It adds no decision right: it moves the time a change shows, never what changes.

One row per request: pending, then stamped by first-light-apply.yml with the pull request it opened or updated. A reviewer sign-in (is_allowed_reviewer()) files a pending row and reads the rows; a trigger blanks every other field on insert, a unique index allows one pending request at a time, and only the service role (the workflow) updates a row; nobody deletes. No new decision right: a request asks for a pull request, and Sam's merge of it is the decision. No student data: a request carries only the requester's sign-in email and the pull request's link.
dismissed.table:first_light_marks: The First Light tab's marks (Sam, 2026-11-12, #3153: "add a cobi tab so I can edit it"; design #3153 comments 6826461825 and 6829695812). One insert-only row per mark: a painting or photo, keep, drop, add or a position, the collection it came from, and who and when, stamped by trigger from the sign-in. Read and added only by a reviewer sign-in (is_allowed_reviewer(), the rung of the tab's cobi_nav row); no update or delete is granted to anyone, so a newer mark is the only change and the history stays. No new decision right: a mark changes nothing on its own. The change happens only when Sam merges the pull request that first-light-apply.yml opens from the marks, so the decision stays his merge, recorded on GitHub. Disclosure: no student data. A row names a public-domain painting on Wikimedia Commons, a hero photo already in the repo, or a My CPL Story photo MAP already publishes at map.rccd.edu/cplstories, plus the reviewer's sign-in email, so the student-detail disclosure ADR does not reach it; a Drop mark is the takedown path for a story photo.
dismissed.function:library-revise-draft: The edge function that drafts a Library page's revision from its card (Sam, 2026-11-05: "Build it"). It takes the team phrase or a reviewer sign-in and reads and writes with that same credential, so cpl_library's and cpl_library_drafts' policies decide what it may touch and the history trigger files the prior record (Rule 10 a2); it holds no service key. It reads the piece's public copy from GitHub Pages, sends it, the changes typed and any pasted document to the Anthropic API for one call, applies the edits only when each names a passage that occurs once, and stores the draft. Since 2026-11-10 (Sam: "all the way to posting in the public library") it also drafts a Requested piece's first page from a starter page in the public library's look, with the same credential and the same two tables; library-publish makes its library/<slug>/ folder once a person presses Publish it, and List publicly stays the existing switch. It fetches a Google Docs, Slides or Sheets link's plain-text export (docs.google.com only, built from the file id; a private file answers with a sign-in page and is named as not opened). It publishes nothing. Pasted documents leave the database for the model call, the same reach alt-text-draft and slide-script-draft already have; the tab's help says never a student's record. No new decision right: the person who presses Draft it now is the one who asked for the change.
dismissed.workflow:library-publish.yml: Publishes the Library drafts a person approved on their card (Sam, 2026-11-05: "Build it"), every three hours or on dispatch. With the service key it reads only records whose regen carries a draft from the card and an approval (Replace the public copy, or a request to replace at once), writes each draft to library/<slug>/index.html with a receipt of the record's before-values (kb/receipts/library_publish/), commits both to main under the daily-dashboard concurrency group, then moves each record with an update guarded on the updated_at it read, so an edit made on the card since wins. It is the outward step, and it waits on a person's press: the decision to replace a public copy stays with whoever approves the draft, which the record keeps; the workflow only carries it out. Reversible: git revert of the page's commit, and the receipt's before-values (cpl_library_history files the prior row too).
dismissed.function:library-publish-now: The Library card's Publish now (Sam, in session, 2026-11-12: "would be nice to have a manual dispatch button in the library for things we need to push right away"; S642). Reads no table and writes nothing; its one action is dispatching library-publish.yml on main, a run that workflow already allows on dispatch, for a signed-in reviewer only (rpc/is_allowed_reviewer, the check docket-process uses; the team phrase and the anon key are refused), with a token the browser never holds (LIBRARY_DISPATCH_TOKEN, else WORKPLAN_DISPATCH_TOKEN). The workflow file and the ref are fixed in the function and the caller sends nothing; a run already waiting is reused, at most one dispatch starts every two minutes, and it starts nothing while another workflow's run waits in the shared daily-dashboard concurrency group, which a new run would cancel (COBIx on #3171). It grants no new publishing power: the run publishes only drafts a person approved on their card (Publish it or Replace the public copy), so the decision stays with whoever approved the draft and the press moves only when the approved page goes up. What runs is bounded by workflow:library-publish.yml's own entry.
dismissed.workflow:cobix-review.yml: COBIx as a CI reviewer (Sam, 2026-11-05: a workflow so COBIx comments on PRs without him relaying). Comment-only: pull-requests write, no code write, no merge; off until COBIX_REVIEW_ENABLED is true and the endpoint secrets exist. A finding it posts is a claim for Claude Code to verify, never a go or an approval. COBIx's identity is the cobi-cto account (Triage, comment-only, event-driven; 2026-11-05); the Governance register row (scope, what it may do, who revokes it) is the open step, and this entry moves to mapped when it lands. docs/reference/cobix_pr_loop.md
dismissed.table:team_pass_attempts: Failed team-phrase unlocks per request IP (security step 2, Sam's go 2026-11-05 ~22:15Z). Written only by the SECURITY DEFINER team_pass_verify(); no API role reads or writes it (RLS on, no policy, privileges revoked). It holds an IP, a count and two times, no student or staff detail, and expires after a day. It locks an IP for 15 minutes after 8 failures in 10 minutes; no decision right moves, so it needs no register row.
dismissed.rpc:team_pass_verify: The explicit unlock (security step 2): the phrase in x-team-pass, the site in the body; records failures in team_pass_attempts. Same audience and answer as team_pass_ok(), with a lockout; no new decision right.
dismissed.rpc:credential_priority_counts: A read, and an aggregate one: the count of public requests to prioritize each credential (credential and n), open to anon on purpose so the Credential Catalog shows the count beside the credential (Sam, Sheet 162: the count is the signal). It returns no row-level field: the optional email, college and note stay behind the team phrase. A count of asks is not a count of students, so the k=10 rule of adr-student-detail-aggregate-disclosure-control does not reach it. The decision right is DR-31's; the read changes nothing.
dismissed.rpc:credential_submissions_verified: A read of verified rows only: the name, issuer, kind and link a signed-in reviewer verified, with the count of asks, open to anon on purpose so a verified submission joins the Credential Catalog as Not yet evaluated (Sam, 2026-11-06: "yes, build the add your credential route"). It returns nothing waiting or declined and no field a visitor typed about themselves (college, email, note). The decision right is DR-32's; the read changes nothing.
dismissed.workflow:chatbox-ghost-delete.yml: The first DELETE path on chatbox_credentials (Sierra's credential table), though not its first writer: credential-catalog-sync.yml upserts it nightly and stays its one writer of rows; this dispatch-only workflow (kb/_chatbox_ghost_delete.py) only removes rows whose unified_title credential_reference_data.js no longer holds. It adds no decision right: which titles are canonical is decided where the reference is built (DR-34, through the rename and fold applies), what Sierra says is DR-11, and the delete itself is Sam's ruling (Open Asks Sheet 183 card 6, 2026-11-12, "delete"; cpl_memory d-sheet-183-replies-2026-11-12). Each run is a reviewed plan with the full before-rows in kb/receipts/chatbox_ghost_delete_<UTC>/plan.json and an undo that re-inserts them (Rule 10 a2). Disclosure (adr-student-detail-aggregate-disclosure-control): the table holds aggregate credential rows only, students_served inherited from the published reference with served_suppressed already applied, no student-level field. The receipt commits the ghosts' before-rows to this public repo: aggregate credential rows as the sync wrote them from an earlier published reference, small-cell suppression already applied, which the current reference no longer carries. plan checks that claim rather than assuming it: it writes no receipt when any ghost's before-row carries a students_served count from 1 to 9 (the ADR's k = 10) or served_suppressed true with a count (S642, tests/chatbox_ghost_delete_test.py).
dismissed.script:kb/_chatbox_ghost_delete.py: The writer behind workflow:chatbox-ghost-delete.yml (dismissed above with its reason). Its apply refuses unless the plan is committed on origin/main, so a delete runs from that dispatch-only workflow (a plan or an undo may also run by hand with the service key); no schedule calls it, and the sync imports it only to print a count of ghost rows.
